scope: Optional ML research, explicitly separated from production DSP implementation by user choice. No training, model adoption or production dependency is authorized by these backlog entries.

proposal_and_constraints: ML is most sensible as offline fitting of these parameters to a measured room; retain a bounded deterministic renderer.
A small neural residual-echo suppressor/nonlinear front end is a credible hybrid candidate [hybrid AEC research][R3]; keep adaptive cancellation and safe bypass operational without inference.
Classical regularized/layout-aware decoding is preferable to ML replacing the normative decoder.
Learned personalization may choose an HRTF/layout correction offline, with explicit normalization and energy constraints.
Learned models are appropriate only when trained and validated against identified hardware and operating levels, not as an automatic replacement for all coloration.
ML fitting is useful offline for matching measured hardware response/color; it is unnecessary for ordinary parametric EQ.
If neural coloration is added, keep the ceiling mechanism explicit and deterministic; learned release suggestions must never replace the safety bound.
Neural speech/noise masks can estimate covariances, but require a confidence fallback and a strict latency budget rather than replacing the bounded beamformer.
ML HRTF selection from measurements/preferences is plausible offline; online inference must not delay head tracking unpredictably.
ML belongs in optional offline IR denoising/estimation, with measured response preserved and model output validated.
ML personalization may select settings offline; it is not needed in this low-cost deterministic path.

items.proposal_and_constraints: A small speech-conditioned sibilance classifier could gate the existing detector. Measure false positives on music and use confidence-based fallback. Classical relative band-energy detection and hysteresis are alternatives to benchmark before model adoption. Current recorded-sound baseline: audit/artifacts/plugin-audit-20261018/de-esser-recorded.json. This five-recording, single-phoneme-speaker set establishes conditional attenuation, not adequate training data or population accuracy. At the fixed high-gain setting, Wideband attenuates violin by 5.691 dB and cymbal by 5.038 dB; the production detector is based on absolute band level rather than speech identity.

proposal_and_constraints: ML is sensible as a transient/click discriminator or constrained inpainting experiment, with false-positive damage measured explicitly.
A learned music mask is plausible, but speech-trained models should not be assumed safe for arbitrary music; evaluate removal artifacts and latency against the existing path.
Learned source-aware remixing should be a separate optional product mode, not a hidden change to deterministic downmix.
ML can propose settings offline; the runtime gain envelope should remain transparent and bounded.
ML can fit target responses or propose bands offline; it should not replace exact filter realization.
ML/VAD gating is useful only as an explicit speech mode with false-cut and latency evaluation, not as a replacement for a general-purpose gate.
ML may classify safe noise-only intervals on a worker; avoid silently learning program material as noise.
ML may recommend release characteristics, but a learned model should never be the only ceiling enforcement mechanism.
ML filter fitting can run offline; runtime filtering should remain a validated FIR operation.
Classical calibrated equal-loudness compensation is preferable to a learned black box.
ML can fit a user's preference curve from controlled listening data, with uncertainty and gain bounds; it cannot infer acoustic calibration from PCM alone.
This is exact linear algebra; ML is unnecessary except an offline routing suggestion that remains reviewable.

items.plugin: Multiband compressor and single-band compressor alias
proposal_and_constraints: ML is suitable for offline parameter assistance or optional measured-hardware emulation, not opaque automatic loudness changes.

items.plugin: Multiband expander and single-band expander alias
proposal_and_constraints: A learned mask is reasonable for an explicit denoising mode; preserve the predictable dynamics mode as a baseline.

A monophonic learned pitch estimator such as CREPE [CREPE][R5] is a candidate only for supported material; test confidence gating and do not treat it as a general polyphonic reference-frequency oracle.
Neural emulation is useful for a measured nonlinear target, with alias and parameter-sweep tests rather than waveform similarity alone.
A learned target mask is plausible for a separate restoration mode; compare latency and artifacts to the classical compressor first.
ML scene classification could suggest settings offline, but real-time width decisions should remain predictable.
Initialize updates coefficients but reset clears history; callers must not assume reinitialize resets learned envelope state.
ML onset classification can assist difficult material, but should only modulate bounded controls with an independent deterministic fallback.
ML source masks are a meaningful optional improvement only with measured extra latency, leakage/artifact metrics and graceful fallback.
ML can estimate position or personalize transfer functions off the critical path; constrain the inverse filter's gain and retain measured validation.
